text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- European Commission approves merger of Boeing and McDonnell Douglas in principle after Boeing promie to give up on exclusive supply contracts with three U.S. airlines.
-- Blue-chip CAC 40 index soared above 3,000 yesterday.
-- Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said he sees French unemployment rate remaining at the same level for some time and decreasing at the end of 1998.
-- LVMH buys perfume retailer Sephora for 1.6 billion francs.
-- GAN puts nits UIC and UIS up for sale.
-- Deutsche Bank interested in developing asset management activities in France.
-- Packaging group Sidel and bottling assembly lines maker Gebo merge to create group with annual turnover of 4.6 billion francs.
LA TRIBUNE
-- Deutsche Bank chairman's talk of buying a banking network in France triggered rise in French banking sector shares.
-- Generale des Eaux considers pulling out of street signs and furniture firm Decaux.
L'AGEFI
-- A hike in tax on corporate profits is expected to cost some 350 million francs a year to banks, on their French activity, according to French banks association AFB.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Franc being underpriced by 20 percent against the dollar, and current low interest rates mean an exceptional opportunity for French economy to grow.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- European Commission agrees to Boeing McDonnell Dougles merger.
-- Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn does not rule out curbing public deficits to three percent of GDP in 1997, he told German daily Die Zeit.
-- 1998 Finance Act to be presented to cabinet on September 24.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- Europeans agree to Boeing merger.
-- LVMH brought its stakes in GrandMet and Guinness to above ten percent, allowing LVMH to call special shareholders meetings if they reject its merger plan.
